misconception_description: Student believes that colons (:) are used for variable assignment.

solutions.generated_code:
program JumlahMinMaks
kamus
  n, i, x, minimum, maksimum : integer
algoritma
  input(n)
  for i <- 1 to n do
    input(x)
    if i == 1 then
      minimum : x
      maksimum : x
    else
      if x < minimum then
        minimum : x
      endif
      if x > maksimum then
        maksimum : x
      endif
    endif
  endfor
  output(minimum + maksimum)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student replaced the assignment operator (=) with a colon (:), believing this is how to assign values to variables in Python. From the student's perspective, they are correctly storing the result of max(nums)+min(nums) in the variable sum. In reality, this creates a type annotation without assignment, so sum remains undefined. When the function tries to return sum, it will raise a NameError because sum was never actually assigned a value. The student has no reason to suspect this won't work - they believe : is the proper assignment syntax.
